text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

Abstract
We queried NCBI GEO to determine the scope of GSE309890 and to enumerate its downloadable files. Using the GEO Series accession “GSE309890” with a request to list supplementary files, we retrieved the study metadata, organism, experiment type, platform, sample count, FTP directory paths, and the exact supplementary file entries. The record is an Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 RNA-seq expression profiling study titled “Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback.” Key figures from the record include 6 samples and 1 supplementary file (GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz; 510K) available from GEO’s FTP. No PubMed links are registered for this Series at GEO. The result matters because GEO stores processed expression matrices in supplementary files, not within the API response; identifying the specific downloadable file and its location is necessary for reanalysis and reuse. The output provides the precise FTP URLs and file metadata, enabling immediate data acquisition and downstream processing.

I. Introduction
Background. GSE309890 is a GEO Series in Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 that investigates how the SSRI sertraline biases antibiotic resistance emergence via redox and metabolic rewiring, focusing on the pentose phosphate pathway and transketolase A (tktA). The study uses expression profiling by high-throughput sequencing (RNA-seq).
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. The exact study description and which processed files are downloadable from GEO were not established.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Identify what GSE309890 is about and list the files available for download. Expectation: The GEO Series record will include a summary and supplementary file(s) containing processed expression values with direct FTP links.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We targeted GEO because it is the authoritative source of processed expression matrices and Series-level metadata. We used a Series accession to retrieve structured metadata and file listings.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO (accessed via functions.geo_series).
Procedures.
- functions.geo_series with arguments: accession="GSE309890", list_files=true.
This returned the Series metadata (title, summary, taxon, experiment type, date, platform, sample list, BioProject, GEO page URL), the FTP directory, and the supplementary files with name, size, last-modified timestamp, and direct URL.
Statistical Analysis.
- Sample count was taken directly from record.sample_count.
- Supplementary file count is the length of the returned supplementary_files list.
- File sizes and timestamps were read from the supplementary_files fields.
No deduplication was required; all counts reflect the GEO record fields.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Study metadata for GSE309890.
| Field            | Value                                                                 |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Accession        | GSE309890                                                              |
| Title            | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Organism         | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655                              |
| Experiment type  | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing                     |
| Date public      | 2026/02/01                                                             |
| Platform         | GPL24659                                                               |
| Sample count     | 6                                                                      |
| BioProject       | PRJNA1363958                                                           |
| GEO page URL     | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890          |
| FTP directory    | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/          |

Table 2. Downloadable supplementary files.
| Name                              | Size | Last modified        | URL                                                                                               |
|-----------------------------------|------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510K | 2025-11-14 11:10     | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz |

Findings.
- The Series reports 6 samples.
- The supplementary_files list contains 1 entry.
- The single downloadable file is a gzipped CSV of FPKMs across all samples.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The Series describes sertraline-induced metabolic rewiring affecting resistance emergence in E. coli and provides a processed FPKM matrix for all samples. The objective is met: we identified the study’s subject and the exact downloadable file.
Context. GEO’s Series record provides the overview and the FTP path. The absence of PubMed links indicates no registered literature in GEO for this Series.
Limitations. GEO’s API returns metadata only; processed expression values must be downloaded from the listed FTP supplementary files. Only one supplementary file is listed. The record does not include raw RNA-seq reads or sample-level alignments; those would be outside GEO’s Series metadata.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 is an E. coli RNA-seq study on SSRI-driven resistance mechanisms, with one downloadable processed FPKM matrix. A next query worth running is to retrieve raw sequencing data via the linked BioProject (PRJNA1363958) from SRA/ENA for alignment-based reanalysis.

References
[1] NCBI GEO Series page: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] NCBI GEO supplementary directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[4] NCBI GEO supplementary file (FPKM matrix): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[5] NCBI Entrez E-utilities esummary call (GDS): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0

Acknowledgments
We thank NCBI GEO and NCBI Entrez E-utilities for providing the Series metadata and file listings.
